messages:
alex.r: FYI NovaHealth started seeing a barrage of 429s on their dedicated pool ~10:03 PST after we pushed the quota migration. Traffic volume looks normal for them but they're being throttled hard.
ops-bot: Created incident INC-7821 for channel support / priority: high :rotating_light:

maria.s: Can you paste the error body and the quota config we gave them? Need to check units.

alex.r: Error sample from their client:
```json
{
  "status":429,
  "error":"rate_limit_exceeded",
  "allowed":5000,
  "window":60,
  "window_unit":"seconds"
}
```
They reported this began immediately after we ran tenant-quota-migrate.

raj: Hmm — migration script recently changed to store window as seconds for internal consistency, but the dedicated rate adapter expects minutes. If true that would shrink the effective throughput by 60x.

kevin: Checking audit logs for the migration now. One sec.

kevin: Confirmed: payload we wrote for tenant novahealth: `{"limit":5000,"window":60,"window_unit":"seconds"}` — previous format was `window_unit: minutes`.

maria.s: That explains it. They asked for 5k tokens/min but got 5k tokens/60s -> actually 5k/1min is same as 5k/60s so wait — clarify math.

raj: Quick math: the adapter interprets `window_unit` values as `minutes|hours` only. When it saw `seconds` it treated it as `minutes` fallback in older code path? Long story short, our dedicated rate calculator divides by window *assuming minutes. If we store 60 with unit seconds but reader treats it as minutes, effective window becomes 60 minutes instead of 60 seconds -> throughput is 60x smaller. So they hit 429s.

alex.r: Ok. So migration wrote `seconds` and adapter treated it like minutes -> major throttling.

support-lead: Recommended mitigation: 1) temporary override to bump limit for NovaHealth on the dedicated pool; 2) hotfix reader to accept seconds; 3) backfill correct unit in DB. Which do we want first?

maria.s: Do 1) now to stop customer impact. I'll coordinate the communication.

kevin: Applying temporary override via admin API now: `POST /admin/tenants/novahealth/overrides {"limit":300000,"window":1,"window_unit":"minutes"}` — TTL 2 hours.

ops-bot: admin API call succeeded (request id abc-123).

alex.r: NovaHealth reports errors dropping within 60s, latency back to normal :white_check_mark: they say no more 429s.

raj: I'll cut a small patch to the dedicated rate adapter to handle `seconds` and `minutes` explicitly and add defensive validation. Will deploy canary to one pool.

kevin: Added DB backfill job to rewrite any `window_unit: "seconds"` into `minutes` where `window` >= 60 and confirmed query scope limited to tenant quota table. Running now (job id backfill-173000).

maria.s: Customer update drafted: explained root cause (unit mismatch from migration), steps taken (temporary override + backfill + patch) and ETA for permanent fix (2h). Sending.

support-lead: Postmortem owners: raj (fix), kevin (backfill + migrator check), maria.s (customer comms). Add monitoring: alert when >5% of tenants have `window_unit` not in allowed set.

alex.r: Thanks team. Closing this thread once backfill and canary look clean.

kevin: Backfill finished, 84 tenants had `seconds` -> converted to `minutes`. Canary patch deployed to canary pool, looks stable.

raj: Patch merged to main, scheduled rollout. I'll open the PR with tests for unit-handling.

maria.s: Customer confirmed recovered and appreciates the quick fix. :tada:

support-lead: Marking incident resolved and will draft postmortem for next ops review.

ops-bot: INC-7821 status -> resolved.
